Captain of the reborn Band of the Hawk's archers.

His stone-hard hide takes a direct strike from the Dragon Slayer without damage.
Beaten when Guts plants explosives in an existing crack, which Mozgus ignites himself.
Astral projects into Guts' mind to pry him loose from the Berserker Armor.
Calls the Lady of the Deep Water and floods Enoch Village.
Works the Wheel of Flame against massed opponents.
Leads the Band of the Hawk after Griffith's capture, preventing its annihilation.

Stabs an apostle in the jaw at the Eclipse to free Judeau.
Engages only after securing terrain that offsets an opponent's strength.
Holds Guts in a one-sided duel where Guts can barely see and cannot draw his weapons.
Admits he could never beat Guts in a fight on even terms.
Commands the Holy Iron Chain Knights and takes part in burning heretics.
Studies magic under Schierke and fights alongside her with it.
Kills birds with thrown rocks, then frees Farnese and Casca by throwing one at a troll.
Fights with the Salamander Dagger, forged in lava, paired with a cutlass.

Has an armourer make a hand of gold with mother-of-pearl nails to strap to the stump, sturdy enough to buckle a shield to.
Fights Brienne of Tarth on a bridge with his wrists still manacled after a year in a cell, comes close several times, and is worn down.
Held over a tree stump by Locke's men and relieved of his sword hand with a carving knife.
Cut his way through the Golden Company to reach Maelys the Monstrous and slew him in single combat during the War of the Ninepenny Kings.
The killing of Maelys made his name known across the Seven Kingdoms.
Climbed the walls of Duskendale and the Dun Fort disguised as a beggar, killed a sentry, freed Aerys II from the dungeon, and cut down Ser Symon Hollard and two guards getting him out.
Took an arrow in the chest during that rescue.
Won his knighthood at sixteen from Aegon V, riding as a mystery knight and unhorsing Prince Duncan and Ser Duncan the Tall.
Rescued Lady Jeyne Swann and her septa from the Kingswood Brotherhood, and killed its leader Ser Simon Toyne in single combat.
The White Book records him wounded by arrow, spear and sword at the Battle of the Trident, fighting beside his Sworn Brothers and Rhaegar.
Killed a dozen friends of Robert Baratheon and Eddard Stark on the Trident, and Robert sent his own maester rather than let Roose Bolton cut his throat.
Won the championship of a tourney at King's Landing at fifty-seven, and unhorsed Sandor Clegane in a tilt at a tourney in 297 AC.
Beats two men thirty and forty years his junior in his first two contests of the Hand's tourney, then loses to Jaime Lannister on the third tilt.
Dismissed from the Kingsguard by Joffrey's council for being old, he throws down his sword in the throne room and walks out.
Recalls killing two of the gold cloaks sent to seize him in the stables, unarmed, and getting clear of the Red Keep.
Kills Khrazz, a pit fighter of great speed with an arakh, taking several wounds before he opens the man's belly and finishes him through the heart.
Publicly dismissed by Joffrey, he strips off cloak and breastplate in front of the laughing court and says he will die a knight.
Draws several of the ambushers off a wounded Grey Worm in a Meereenese alley, cuts down a number of them, and dies of the stab wounds.
Winterfell whispered of him as the deadliest of the seven knights of Aerys II's Kingsguard, slain by their young lord in single combat.
Eddard Stark told Bran he was the finest knight he ever saw, fought with a blade forged from a fallen star, and would have killed him but for Howland Reed.
Jaime tells Loras Tyrell and four other Kingsguard that Arthur could have slain all five of them with his left hand while pissing with the right.
Jaime recalls that Arthur was the stronger of the two of them.
Killed the Smiling Knight in single combat to finish the Kingswood campaign, and knighted Jaime Lannister for valour in the field afterwards.
Held the title Sword of the Morning, and the recorded history has him killed by Eddard Stark in single combat at the tower of joy.
Many held him to have been the most chivalrous warrior in the Seven Kingdoms.
Eddard's fever dream puts him in front of the tower of joy with Dawn slung across his back, and the dream breaks off as the fighting starts.
Remembered as splendid, and beaten by Rhaegar Targaryen at the tourney at Harrenhal.
Broke twelve lances against Rhaegar at another tourney and still lost the tilt.
Joffrey goes through his page in the Book of Brothers — the kingswood campaign, the Smiling Knight killed in single combat, and a spell in temporary command of the Kingsguard.
In the vision Bran Stark is shown he fights with a sword in each hand, cuts down most of Eddard Stark's companions, disarms Eddard, and is stabbed in the back of the neck by Howland Reed.
Waymar Royce, killed by the Others in the haunted forest, gets to his feet with blue eyes and kills Will.
Othor's corpse rises inside Castle Black and goes for Jeor Mormont in his own chamber; Jon Snow sets it alight and the fire ends it.
The second corpse brought in from beyond the Wall killed five men, among them Ser Jaremy Rykker, whose own dagger did it.
Alliser Thorne tells the court the severed hand he carried from Castle Black was still moving when he set out.
Tyrion keeps him waiting long enough that what he finally produces is a jar of bones.
Samwell Tarly, recalling the horde that broke the great ranging on the Fist, saw a dead bear among them.
Samwell's dragonglass dagger shatters on Small Paul's mail, and he destroys the thing with a burning brand instead.
Melisandre tells Samwell that necromancy animates them but they remain dead flesh, and that steel and fire will serve.
Summer eats the flesh from a severed arm that is still grasping, and it stops moving once the direwolf cracks the bone open.
Tormund's son Torwynd dies of the cold days after the battle beneath the Wall, rises, and his father has to put him down.
Everyone killed in the massacre stands up together as the ships pull away; some five thousand wildlings get out on the ships, and at least as many are left on the shore to rise.

The captured one charges Cersei Lannister and is hauled up short by its chain; Sandor Clegane cuts it in two when it turns on him, the upper half crawls at him, and he severs a hand, which Jon Snow burns with a torch before finishing the wight with dragonglass.
They throw themselves into the burning trench around Winterfell until their bodies smother it and the rest of the column crosses.
The dead sealed in Winterfell's crypts break out through the walls and attack the people sheltering there.
Tells Sansa that Gregor shoved the side of his face into the coals of a brazier — "I was younger than you, six, maybe seven" — and held him there until three grown men pulled him off.
Unhorses Renly Baratheon on the first day of the Hand's tourney.
Beats Jaime Lannister on the second pass after nearly losing the first, and Jaime is led off the field unable to see through his mangled helm.

Steps between Gregor and the downed Loras Tyrell, stops the savage blows Gregor then aims at Sandor's hound's-head helm without once cutting at his brother's unprotected face, kneels when King Robert shouts, and is given the championship by Loras without a final tilt.
Jaime rates him among the strongest men alive in Westeros, and believes his own speed and skill would be the answer to it.
Kills Cayn among Eddard Stark's household guard during the arrest in the Red Keep.
Cuts the rioting crowd away from Sansa Stark when she is nearly pulled from the saddle, and gets her back inside the walls.
Fights Beric Dondarrion's burning sword in the hollow hill with his own shield alight and strapped to his arm, and cuts through blade, mail and shoulder.
Kills several mounted Frey men outside the castle during the Red Wedding, in the mud and floodwater among the burning pavilions, and knocks Arya Stark senseless to stop her running back into it.
Kills Polliver at the inn at the crossroads and holds off the Tickler until Arya finishes him, coming out of it wounded in the thigh, ribs, neck and face, with the stump of his burned ear sliced off.
Begs Arya for the gift of mercy as the wounds go bad, and she leaves him under a tree beside the Trident.
The Elder Brother of the Quiet Isle tells Brienne he buried the man himself, and that at the end he wept from the pain and asked for a quick death.
Steps between Gregor and the unhorsed Loras Tyrell, trades blows with his brother, and stops the moment Robert orders it.
With his shield on fire he cuts through Beric Dondarrion's flaming sword, armour and shoulder, and Thoros of Myr prays the man back afterwards.
Takes on five of Gregor's men alone in a taproom and, put on the floor with a dagger at his own throat, forces the hand aside and drives the man's head onto his own blade over and over.
Loses a hand-to-hand fight to Brienne of Tarth, who bites off part of his ear, batters him with a rock and puts him over a cliff edge.
At sixteen he fought Lord Edgar Yronwood over the man's paramour; the duel was to first blood, both took cuts, and Yronwood's festered and killed him.
Rumour that he fought that duel with a poisoned blade is where the name Red Viper comes from, among friends and enemies alike.
Doran recalls him toppling much larger boys at the shoulder-riding game in the Water Gardens, and Oberyn promising on leaving Sunspear to do it again.
Chooses light armour and a turned ash spear eight feet long for the trial by battle, and warns Tyrion the night before not to touch the weapon.
Wounds Gregor Clegane repeatedly at the chinks of his plate, severs his hamstring after the bigger man tires of the chase, and breaks the spear off in his belly.
With Gregor down, he refuses to finish him and demands a confession instead; Gregor trips him, smashes out his teeth and eyes and caves in his skull.
Cersei reports to her own small council that Gregor Clegane has died of the poison, months after the trial, and the cleaned skull is boxed for Sunspear.
Tyene Sand tells her sisters she knows the poison her father used, without ever naming it, and that if his spear so much as broke the Mountain's skin then Clegane is dead however big he was.
Qyburn identifies it as manticore venom thickened by a spell to draw out the dying, over Pycelle's objection that manticore venom kills on the instant.
Struck Willas Tyrell's breastplate clean in a tourney; the boy's foot caught in a stirrup and his horse came down on him, crippling him for life.
Doran tells the Sand Snakes that Oberyn was ever the viper — deadly, dangerous, unpredictable — and that no man dared tread on him, while he himself was only the grass that hid him.
Circles the Mountain with a spear for the length of the duel, opens him repeatedly, brings him down, and is caught by the leg while standing over him demanding the confession.
Warned at sixteen by Ser Humfrey Wagstaff that he would expect a proper woman, she said she would accept it from a man who could beat her, and broke three of his bones trying.
Wins the melee at Bitterbridge with a morningstar, beating Loras Tyrell and many of the knights who had been wagering on her maidenhead, and asks for the rainbow cloak as her prize.
Accused of Renly's murder with her own sword out of reach, she fends off Ser Emmon Cuy with the dead king's blade.
Scales a cliff above the Red Fork and rolls a boulder onto Ser Robin Ryger's galley to throw off the pursuit from Riverrun.
Fighting the manacled and long-starved Jaime Lannister on the Duskendale road, she proves the stronger of the two and holds his head under the water.
Thrown into the bear pit at Harrenhal in a gown with nothing but a tourney sword, she keeps the animal off until Jaime Lannister comes back for her.
Kills Pyg and Timeon of the Brave Companions with Oathkeeper at the Whispers, then kills Shagwell after making him dig a grave.
Outnumbered at the inn at the crossroads and defending the orphans there, she kills Rorge, and Biter chews the flesh from her cheek.
Gendry kills Biter with a spear before she bleeds out, and she is taken prisoner by the brotherhood without banners while delirious.

Loses her sword and keeps going, biting a piece out of Sandor Clegane's ear and beating him with a rock until he goes over the cliffside.

claim: Offers to yield at the Butcher's Ball if his men are spared, is refused, challenges all three enemy commanders to single combat, and is put down by Red Robb Rivers and two of his longbowmen with one arrow each before he can fight any of them.
Unhorses Daemon Targaryen in the lists at Viserys I's tourney, then beats him a second time on foot when the prince sends for Dark Sister.
Beats Ser Joffrey Lonmouth to death with bare fists in the middle of the wedding feast, snapping the man's arm when he draws a dagger, and stops only when he can no longer lift his own.
Forces Lord Lyman Beesbury back into his chair hard enough to crack the old man's skull on the council table, then draws on the Lord Commander of the Kingsguard.
Disarms Ser Arryk Cargyll in a duel outside the Grand Sept while Aemond runs his brother down and pins him, the king-to-be pleading to be let go throughout.
His oiled braid, hung with tiny silver bells, falls past his waist to his thighs, and marks him among the Dothraki as an undefeated warlord.
Viserys tells Daenerys that the length of that braid means the man has never been defeated in combat.
Thirty years old, moving like a panther, and younger than Daenerys had expected.
Leads a khalasar of forty thousand warriors, the largest on the Dothraki sea.
Melts his belt of gold medallions and pours the pot over Viserys Targaryen's head, killing him without spilling blood in Vaes Dothrak.
Returns to Vaes Dothrak with a hrakkar's carcass across a packhorse and the scar it left down his leg.
Jorah Mormont brings word that he has killed Khal Ogo and Ogo's son Fogo with only minor wounds, and Drogo repeats the boast himself.
Daenerys finds him with an arrow through the arm and an arakh cut that has taken off one of his nipples, and he calls them scratches.
The wound festers after he tears away the maegi's poultice, and he falls from his horse in front of the khalasar.
Left breathing and vacant by the blood magic, he is smothered with a pillow by Daenerys.
Throws his arakh down before answering Mago's challenge, takes the cut across the chest without guarding, opens the man's throat with his own blade and pulls his tongue out through the wound.
The cut Mago gave him festers under Mirri Maz Duur's care until he can no longer keep his seat.
Catelyn Stark was particularly annoyed on the occasions when he bested Robb at their training.
Sets fire to the corpse standing over Jeor Mormont in the Lord Commander's chamber and burns himself badly doing it.
His right hand is swathed in silk halfway to the elbow afterwards and carries the burn scars from that night.
Kills Qhorin Halfhand with Longclaw in front of Rattleshirt's hunters, but only after Ghost bites the ranger's calf and gives him the opening.
Pours boiling oil down on the Thenns coming up into the King's Tower and blocks the trap door with the iron kettle.
Takes over the defence of the Wall after Donal Noye is killed at the gate, and holds it for days against Mance Rayder's host.
Beheads Janos Slynt himself with Longclaw for refusing an order, rather than hanging him as first commanded.
Asks three of Iron Emmett's best to come at him together, and is beaten instead by Rattleshirt, who is fighting with a greatsword and no shield and ends the bout on top of him.
Stabbed in turn by Bowen Marsh, Wick Wittlestick and others in the Castle Black yard, each of them saying "For the Watch."
Both he and the White Walker see Longclaw hold against a crystal blade, and he strikes before it can recover, breaking the thing into ice.
Rides out alone after Rickon is shot, loses his horse to Bolton archers, and stands on foot to meet the cavalry charge.
Trampled by his own retreating infantry and nearly suffocated under the press before he can force his way back up.
Blocks three of Ramsay Bolton's arrows with a Mormont shield, knocks the bow aside and beats him senseless, stopping only when he sees Sansa.
Lured out to a false message and stabbed one at a time by his own brothers of the Night's Watch in the courtyard at Castle Black, the boy Olly last.

Shouts Vhagar down in High Valyrian as she draws breath to burn him, climbs to the saddle and takes her up over High Tide.

Breaks Lucerys Velaryon's nose, shrugs off all four of the children who pin him, has Luke by the throat with a rock in his free hand, then turns on Jacaerys instead — and it is Jacaerys, rock raised over him, who flings sand in his face and gives the loose Lucerys time to take up the dropped knife and open his eye.
Draws a blade on Lucerys and charges him under Borros Baratheon's roof until the lord stops it; in the storm afterwards Vhagar stops obeying him and takes boy and dragon in one bite.

locator: S02E04 “The Red Dragon and the Gold”
claim: Burns his own brother out of the sky at Rook's Rest, then crushes Meleys's neck in Vhagar's jaws and drops Rhaenys onto the castle walls.

Warned by an informer, he rode at once with all his knights and squires, reached Summerhall ahead of the loyalist lords, and beat the hosts of Cafferen, Fell and Grandison in three battles in one day before they could join up, killing Lord Fell in single combat.
Slew Marq Grafton at the taking of Gulltown at the start of the rebellion.
Harwin tells Arya that when the bells rang at Stoney Sept, Robert came out of hiding and "slew six men that day, they say", Ser Myles Mooton among them — hearsay, and marked as such by the teller.
Jon Connington remembers being very nearly killed by him on the steps of the town's sept that day.
The spiked warhammer was forged for him at Storm's End by Donal Noye.

Eddard remembers the two of them circling in the shallows until a crushing blow of the hammer stove in the ruby dragon and the chest beneath, and men of both armies scrabbling for the stones afterwards.
Jaime Lannister reckons him the stronger of the two of them.
Preferred the melee to the lists, where he could hit men with a blunted axe or hammer.
Six and a half feet tall by Eddard's reckoning, and grown at least eight stone in the nine years since Greyjoy's Rebellion.
Too fat for his own armour at the Hand's tourney, he sends Lancel and Tyrek Lannister to Ser Aron Santagar for a breastplate stretcher, and Eddard and Barristan Selmy argue him out of the melee.
Varys tells Eddard afterwards that the queen had arranged for the king to die in that melee.
Brought back to the Red Keep gored open by the boar, he dictates the will and asks for the order on Daenerys Targaryen to be called off.
Varys points out that Lancel Lannister kept the king's wineskin full for the whole of the hunt.

Set on riding in the joust, he torments Lancel Lannister over the armour that will not close and sends him off on an invented errand, and Eddard Stark tells him he is too fat for it and that no knight would dare unhorse him.
Barristan Selmy says the king made everyone stand aside so that he could take the boar by himself.
Eddard's memory of the tourney at Harrenhal has him unhorse Yohn Royce, Brandon Stark and Arthur Dayne, then take the final tilt from Barristan Selmy.
Passed over Elia Martell to set a crown of blue winter roses in Lyanna Stark's lap, which Eddard remembers as the moment all the smiles died.
Cersei, ten years old in the stands at the Lannisport tourney of 276 AC, watched two of her uncles fall before his lance along with a dozen of her father's finest jousters, the flower of the west.
Unhorsed Ser Barristan Selmy at the same tourney, and lost the champion's tilt to Arthur Dayne.
Barristan Selmy tells Daenerys that men said her brother loved his silver-stringed harp better than his lance, and that he never much cared for fighting.
Barristan tells Daenerys her brother was bookish as a child until he read something in a scroll that made him want to be a warrior, after which he trained fiercely.
Told her brother must have been a peerless warrior, Barristan calls him a most puissant one and then answers that "a warrior without peer" are fine words, but words win no battles.
Took command of the royal army after Jon Connington lost at the Bells, leaving Jaime Lannister behind at the Red Keep.
Lay dead in the stream at the ford with his breastplate stove in, while both armies searched the water for the rubies.
Jorah Mormont tells Daenerys that Rhaegar fought valiantly, nobly and honourably on the Trident, and that Rhaegar died.
Eddard, who has cause enough to hate him, will allow only that he did not think Rhaegar frequented brothels.
Appears in one episode of the series and no other, in a vision shown to Bran Stark, marrying Lyanna Stark before a heart tree.
Eddard Stark gives her the sword back and hires Syrio Forel, who throws her a lead-weighted wooden blade she cannot catch and spends four hours letting her fail to strike him.
Kills a stableboy who grabs her arm in the stables during the purge of House Stark, putting Needle through his belly.

At the crossroads inn she stabs the squire in the belly, kills the Tickler from behind with his own dagger while repeating his questions back at him, then recovers Needle from Polliver and finishes the squire.
Asked by the kindly man who killed the deserter Dareon, whose throat was cut and whose body went into a canal, she answers with her own name and is blind by morning.
Kills her first assigned target by slipping a poisoned coin into a shipowner's purse, knowing the old man tests every coin with his teeth.
The series gives her Polliver — she cuts his leg from behind, takes Needle off him and drives it into his throat the way he had killed Lommy.
Spars Brienne of Tarth to a stalemate at Winterfell, switching to a Valyrian steel dagger when Needle is knocked away, and ends with each of them holding a blade at the other's throat.
Cuts Walder Frey's throat at his own table after showing him what she has done with his sons.
Caught by the throat and the left wrist in the godswood, she drops the dagger from one grip into the other and drives it into the Night King, who shatters.
Petyr Baelish says he lost a Valyrian steel dagger to Tyrion Lannister by betting on Jaime at the tourney on Prince Joffrey's name day, because Loras Tyrell unhorsed him.
Robert Baratheon retells the story of the Knight of Flowers unhorsing Jaime Lannister at that earlier tourney, and calls him a son any man would be proud of.
One of the four still standing at the end of the first day of the Hand's tourney, alongside both Cleganes and Jaime Lannister.
Rides a mare in heat against Gregor Clegane's struggling stallion, puts man and mount down with a lance that does not even break, and raises his visor to the crowd.
Gregor Clegane kills his own horse with a single blow that half severs its neck and comes at Loras with a sword, and Sandor Clegane stands over him until the king stops it.
Fights with a longaxe at Renly Baratheon's melee at Bitterbridge and is one of the last two left in it.
Nearly breaks down in the White Sword Tower over Robar Royce and Emmon Cuy, and Jaime Lannister absolves him of having killed the two Rainbow Guard in a rage.
Asks Cersei for the command at Dragonstone and promises her the castle inside a fortnight, and she grants it hoping the walls will kill him.
Aurane Waters reports that Loras took Dragonstone, that boiling oil was poured on him from the walls, that he lay dying, and that he had turned the storming of the keep into a massacre.
Throws Gregor Clegane by riding a mare in heat, and afterwards declares Sandor Clegane the winner of the match rather than himself.
Renounces his name and his claim before the High Sparrow, and the Faith Militant carve a seven-pointed star into his forehead in front of his father and sister.
Arms Tyrion Lannister with a double-bladed axe when the mountain clans come down on the party, telling him to pretend he is splitting logs.
Refuses a shield and fights Ser Vardis Egen in ringmail over boiled leather against full plate, being fifteen years younger, half a hand taller and longer in the reach.
Runs the armoured knight until he tires, opens his elbow while the narrow visor loses him, topples a statue onto him and kills him where he lies.
Lysa Arryn's court insists any knight must beat a common sellsword, and Catelyn Stark, who saw him fight on the high road, is far less sure.
Refuses to stand for Tyrion a second time because the queen's champion would be Gregor Clegane, being newly betrothed to Lollys Stokeworth and well paid by Cersei.
Falyse Stokeworth brings Cersei the account of the duel — Bronn beat Ser Balman Byrch in single combat, made him say who had put him up to it, then killed him and turned her out of the castle.
Fights defensively until Ser Vardis Egen tires inside his armour, wounds and then kills him, and kicks the body out through the Moon Door.
Puts Trystane Martell down in the Water Gardens and holds off Tyene and Nymeria Sand together while Obara drives Jaime Lannister away from Myrcella.
Cuts his way back to Qyburn's scorpion on foot after his horse is hamstrung, crews the weapon alone and puts a bolt through Drogon's shoulder.
Tells Daenerys he earned his knighthood in Greyjoy's Rebellion by following Thoros of Myr through the breach at Pyke.
At Robert Baratheon's tourney outside Lannisport he held Jaime Lannister to a draw in the final joust, took the champion's laurel and named Lynesse Hightower queen of love and beauty.
Entered tourney after tourney afterwards to pay for his wife's tastes and never distinguished himself again, each loss costing him a suit of armour and a charger.
Interrupts a wineseller pressing a cask of Arbor red on Daenerys by demanding a cup of it himself; threatened, the merchant pours two cups, then refuses to drink and throws the cask at her instead.
Fights Qotho bare-headed and is hard pressed until the bloodrider's arakh cuts into his hip and catches on the bone, which gives him the opening to kill the man.
Months later the hip wound from Qotho has still not fully healed, and it only begins to heal once Daenerys tends it herself at Vaes Tolorro.
Fights the Stone Men off the boat in the ruins of Old Valyria and pulls Tyrion out of the water, then finds his own wrist cracking with greyscale.
Outmatched by a Braavosi water dancer in the grand melee at Daznak's Pit and about to be finished, he survives only because a pit fighter kills the Braavosi from behind.
Kills that pit fighter to end the melee as the last man upright, then hurls a spear the length of the arena into a Son of the Harpy creeping up on the royal box.
Fights the wights off Daenerys on the open field at Winterfell after she is thrown from Drogon, and dies of the wounds in her arms.
Bars Obara Sand from Prince Doran's rest at the Water Gardens, and the narration allows that deadly as she is, she is no match for the captain.
Brings the butt of his longaxe down on the marble floor to warn Tyene Sand off the dais when she reaches for Prince Doran.
Steps out of the barge cabin on the Greenblood with a dozen crossbowmen, and Ser Arys Oakheart of the Kingsguard charges them, is hit by several bolts, reaches the deck and falls to the longaxe.

locator: ch. 21 (The Queenmaker) and ch. 40 (The Princess in the Tower)
claim: Orders the horsemen after Ser Gerold Dayne, who has wounded Myrcella Baratheon and fled; the escape itself is confirmed a book later, when Arianne learns Darkstar got away from Hotah's men and is still uncaught.
Watching Ser Balon Swann present the Mountain's skull at Sunspear, he judges that this knight would be harder to put down than Arys Oakheart was.
Brings Prince Doran's guard into the Water Gardens and surrounds the Sand Snakes, Jaime Lannister and Bronn, forcing all of them to drop their weapons without a blow struck.
Tyene Sand stabs him in the back beside Doran Martell's chair and he dies on the spot, while the rest of the prince's guard stands and watches.

Hired as a dancing master, he throws Arya a wooden blade weighted to make her strong, tells her the water dance is not the hacking iron dance of Westeros, and lets her fail to touch him for four hours.
Tells Arya he became First Sword of Braavos because he alone looked at the Sealord's cat and said what it plainly was, where the other bravos saw a marvel.
Breaks the fingers of the first guardsman to draw on him, and by the time Arya reaches the far end of the Small Hall five Lannister men are dead or dying around him.
Lands many blows on Ser Meryn Trant's heavy plate with the practice sword before the knight cuts it in two, and Arya runs without seeing the end.
Cersei Lannister tells Tyrion she sent Meryn Trant to take Arya and the dancing master interfered, so the girl escaped and is likely dead.
Disarms and disables every one of the lightly armoured guardsmen with the wooden practice sword, then faces Meryn Trant and tells Arya that the First Sword of Braavos does not run.
Rides in the procession at the Hand's tourney, where Jeyne Poole announces she would marry him on sight.
Eddard Stark refuses Loras Tyrell the commission and gives it to Beric instead, putting a hundred men under him to bring Gregor Clegane to the king's justice.
Tywin Lannister's army ambushes that party and kills most of it, and word reaching Robb Stark is that Beric may have escaped but nobody knows.
Arya sees what is left of him — one eye gone, part of the skull crushed in, a noose scar at the throat and a terrible wound through the chest.
Cuts open his own palm with the blade to set it alight, then loses the fight when Sandor Clegane splits him from shoulder to breastbone, and is on his feet again before the Hound has left.
Asks Thoros how many times he has been brought back; Thoros answers six, and says the seventh may be the end of them both.
Can no longer remember his own past well enough to find his ancestral seat, and Thoros takes this as proof the Lord of Light is not done with him.
The ghost of High Heart calls him the Lord of Corpses because the stink of the grave on him is fresh.
Thoros tells Brienne that Lord Beric's fire has gone out of this world and a grimmer shadow leads the brotherhood in his place.
Lights the sword with his own blood, sets Sandor Clegane's shield burning, and is cut down through sword, armour and shoulder before Thoros prays him back.
Sets a resurrected snow bear alight with the flaming sword beyond the Wall, and afterwards cauterises Thoros's wounds with the same blade.
Loses the flaming sword and is stabbed repeatedly covering the retreat of Arya Stark and Sandor Clegane through the castle corridors, and dies once the great hall doors are shut.
Jorah Mormont calls the Unsullied the best trained fighting force in the world and tells Daenerys of the Three Thousand of Qohor, who broke a khalasar.
Kraznys mo Nakloz demonstrates in Astapor that the Unsullied obey every command given them and feel hardly any pain, and both Daenerys and Arstan are appalled by what the training costs.
Daenerys buys all eight thousand Unsullied plus every boy still in training, then turns them on the slavers with one word.
Chosen by the other Unsullied as the ablest among them and put under Jorah Mormont to learn command, he keeps the name he was holding when he was freed because he calls it a lucky one.
Ambushed in a Meereenese alley, he loses his helmet, takes a slash to the leg and a dagger in the side, pulls the dagger out of himself and puts it through an attacker's throat.
Leads the Unsullied into Casterly Rock through the sewer, overwhelms the garrison and takes the castle, then works out from a wounded prisoner that it was a trap.
Spears the fleeing Harry Strickland in the back at the gates, then throws his spear into a Lannister captain who had already thrown down his sword, which is where the sack turns into a massacre.

Knocks Criston Cole on his back with one punch in the training yard and pummels him until four Kingsguard drag him off, while Cole never returns a blow and smiles through it.
Dies at Harrenhal in a fire set by Larys Strong's tongueless agents, unable to force the heat-sealed door to his father's chamber before the ceiling comes down on them.
Catelyn recalls the duel — Brandon Stark asked Petyr to yield more than once, and a backhand through his armour below the ribs put him in the water.
Takes back his dagger from Eddard Stark's throat during the arrest, having bribed the gold cloaks to stand with the queen.
Tells Lysa Arryn he has only ever loved one woman, adds "only Cat", and shoves her out the Moon Door.
Sinks to his knees in the Winterfell great hall pleading for his life, and has his throat cut by Arya Stark.
Seats Ser Ilyn Payne, the King's Justice, in the Queen's Ballroom for the duration of the Battle of the Blackwater.
Tells Sansa that Payne is there for the two of them, because she will not let Stannis take them alive.
Has Ser Osney Kettleblack murder the High Septon, and beds him as the reward.
Shaved of every hair and stripped, she walks barefoot from the Great Sept to the Red Keep through a jeering crowd, and breaks down before she reaches the gate.
Destroys the Great Sept of Baelor and everyone inside it with wildfire laid beneath the building, watching from a window across the city.
Tells Tyrion he was sold to a man who drugged him, cut away his manhood and burned it in a brazier, then put him out on the street.
Jaime, waiting in the eunuch's own chambers, forces him at knifepoint to get Tyrion out of the black cells.
Sends a child to fetch Ser Kevan Lannister to Pycelle's chambers, shoots him with a crossbow, apologises, and sets the little birds on him with knives.
Taken in shackles by Grey Worm without resistance and burned by Drogon on the shore at Daenerys's command.

Commands the reserve from the high ground at the battle on the Green Fork, placing Tyrion and the clansmen on the left in the expectation that they will rout.
Tells Tyrion he countenanced Walder Frey's plan for the wedding, to stop the Freys returning to Robb Stark's cause.
Shot through the bowels with a crossbow while sitting on the privy, unarmed, by Tyrion.

Baelish calls her a fearsome old harridan and not near as frail as she pretends.
At Joffrey's wedding she walks with a cane and smiles toothlessly.
Claims to be near deaf when she first has Sansa Stark to supper.
Highgarden falls in a single swift battle and Jaime Lannister finds her sitting alone in her study; she drinks the poisoned wine he pours.
Tells Jaime she killed Joffrey with the strangler, had never seen it work before, and wants Cersei told it was her.

Destroys the Iron Fleet, breaks the scorpions on the walls, and burns King's Landing after its surrender.
Drops on the undead Viserion from above, rams him hard enough to throw the Night King off his back, and forces him to break off by tearing into his neck with his fangs.
Escapes three attempts to capture him, burning most of the men sent and killing four, and vanishes north into the Dothraki sea.
Impaled at Daznak's Pit by Harghaz's spear, kills him by tearing his arm off, and carries Daenerys out of the pit as the first dragonrider in a century and a half.
Already large in 48 AC, with only Balerion and Vhagar larger.

Tyrion, looking at the skulls in the cellar, holds her to have been larger than Vhagar and smaller than Balerion.

Speared through the neck by the Night King and dropped through the ice, then hauled out and raised with a hand laid on his snout.
Brings down the castle at Eastwatch and that stretch of the Wall with blue fire, opening the way south for the dead.

Struck repeatedly by scorpion bolts from Euron Greyjoy's Iron Fleet and killed, falling into Blackwater Bay.
